description: Advertised US prices, read 2026-10-03 from each provider's own pages (Sinch and Phaxio read again 2026-10-07). cards: calls over each SIP trunk preset when Faxbot's own fax engine places or answers the call. providers: cloud fax providers' per-page or per-minute prices. plans: flat monthly plans with nothing charged per fax; a plan's budget is the normal-use budget Faxbot starts it at (pages and faxes a month, and the billing day when the counts start again), never a limit the provider has promised. Prices are advertised starting or typical rates, not quotes; confirm them against your account. Amounts are decimal strings in the card currency. per_call is a charge for each call; number_setup is a one-time charge for each number. A null price or increment means the provider does not publish it. number_rental_monthly on a provider card is the published monthly price of one fax number, null when the provider does not publish it. Documo publishes no fax API price, so it has no card. UK and Australian carrier cards (Gamma, BT One Voice, Telstra SIP Connect) are in their own currency and carry no price, because none is published. A phone system (Avaya) has no card: the carrier behind it bills the calls. reference_plans: plans a provider publishes that Faxbot never adds as a rate card by itself, because the provider prices the API Faxbot uses differently (eFax prices its API by quote in every country); a person can choose one as their own estimate. included_pages and overage_per_page describe the plan; the estimate counts the monthly fee only. receiving_prices: what a carrier charges for receiving, read for the receiving recommendations (shared inbound channels in price tiers, received-call rates by number type, number rental and any monthly trunk fee); they are never added as rate cards. toll_free: what calling a US or Canadian toll-free number (800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877, 888) costs on each route and what the route needs, read when Faxbot dials a recipient's approved toll-free number. reaches is yes, no or not_published. pricing is own (the prices in the entry), same_as_card (the route's own sending card applies, because its published price makes no exception for toll-free numbers) or not_published (the cost stays unknown). caller_id is what caller ID the route needs on a toll-free call: account_number (a number on the account or one the carrier verified), local_number (a valid local US or Canadian number, never a toll-free one) or set (any real number). They are never added as rate cards.

cards.label: Telnyx SIP trunk, US local, outbound
cards.notes: Starting rate. Telnyx bills 60/60: every call is rounded up to whole minutes, with a one-minute minimum. T.38 is listed as free.

cards.label: Telnyx SIP trunk, US local, inbound
cards.notes: Starting rate. Inbound channels are also offered at $12 per channel per month for the first ten channels as an alternative to per-minute billing.

cards.label: SignalWire SIP, US local, outbound
cards.notes: Programmable voice local outbound rate. SignalWire also lists SIP and WebRTC at $0.003 per minute each way; the page does not say whether that applies in addition to the voice rate. Its managed fax product is a separate $0.0095 per minute. No billing increment is published, so a whole-minute assumption is the cautious estimate.

cards.label: SignalWire SIP, US local, inbound
cards.notes: Programmable voice local inbound rate; see the outbound card about the separate SIP rate. No billing increment is published.

cards.label: Sinch Elastic SIP Trunking, US, outbound
cards.notes: Sinch says Elastic SIP Trunking has per-minute rates and monthly number fees but does not show them on its pages without an account. Enter your contracted rates.

cards.label: Sinch Elastic SIP Trunking, US, inbound
cards.notes: Rates are not published; enter your contracted rates.

cards.label: AnveoDirect, US, outbound (Standard route)
cards.notes: AnveoDirect prices each US prefix separately. This is the median interstate rate across the USA rows of its Standard rate sheet; rows range from $0.00051 to $0.04144 per minute, and almost all bill 1/1 (per second). The number is a per-minute US geographic number.

cards.label: AnveoDirect, US metered number, inbound
cards.notes: Per-minute number with ten inbound channels. Prime numbers instead buy channels at $11.25 per month plus $14 setup each. AnveoDirect requires $25 of prepaid funds. The inbound billing increment is not published.

cards.label: Flowroute SIP trunk, US lower 48 and Canada, outbound
cards.notes: Most outbound destinations bill 6/6. The pricing page shows $1.00 per number; an older FAQ says $0.50 per month. Flowroute bills a fax like a voice call of the same length and charges no setup fee.

cards.label: Flowroute SIP trunk, US, inbound
cards.notes: Inbound calls bill in whole minutes, rounded up.

cards.label: Gamma SIP trunk, UK, outbound
cards.notes: Gamma's own page gives only a range, £3 to £150 a month per SIP channel plus £50 to £150 a month service rental, and no per-minute price; Gamma sells through resellers, who set the rates (read October 3, 2026). Enter your reseller's rates.

cards.label: Gamma SIP trunk, UK, inbound
cards.notes: Gamma's own page gives only a range, £3 to £150 a month per SIP channel plus £50 to £150 a month service rental, and no per-minute price; Gamma sells through resellers, who set the rates (read October 3, 2026). Enter your reseller's rates.

cards.label: BT One Voice SIP trunk, UK, outbound
cards.notes: BT prices One Voice SIP trunks in each customer's contract and publishes none (checked October 3, 2026). Enter your contracted rates.

cards.label: BT One Voice SIP trunk, UK, inbound
cards.notes: BT prices One Voice SIP trunks in each customer's contract and publishes none (checked October 3, 2026). Enter your contracted rates.

cards.label: Telstra SIP Connect, Australia, outbound
cards.notes: Telstra's customer terms say SIP Connect charges are set out in your application form, and calls are charged at your BusinessLine Complete or agreed rates; no price is published (section last changed June 3, 2024, read October 3, 2026). Enter your rates.

cards.label: Telstra SIP Connect, Australia, inbound
cards.notes: Telstra's customer terms say SIP Connect charges are set out in your application form, and calls are charged at your BusinessLine Complete or agreed rates; no price is published (section last changed June 3, 2024, read October 3, 2026). Enter your rates.

plans.label: HumbleFax unlimited plan
plans.notes: The HumbleFax FAQ, read October 3, 2026: "$10 per month to send and receive unlimited faxes. You receive your own dedicated local phone number." and "No gimmicks, no hidden fees, no overage charges." Faxes are included in the plan, so Faxbot adds nothing per fax.
plans.includes_number_note: The HumbleFax FAQ, read again October 5, 2026: the plan comes with a dedicated local fax number that receives faxes into your email inbox. The FAQ explains bringing an existing number to HumbleFax but not moving a number away from it.

budget.sentence: Faxbot starts HumbleFax at 200 pages and 50 faxes a month because HumbleFax's terms keep unlimited faxing for normal, individual use without naming a number; this is a cautious start, not a limit HumbleFax has promised to accept.
budget.basis: HumbleFax publishes no monthly number. 200 pages is what individual fax plans include where a number is published (eFax Personal: 200 pages a month, read 2026-10-04); 50 faxes is 200 pages at four pages a fax. The administrator sets the real budget.
budget.terms_quote: "For individual, non-commercial use, we offer unlimited faxing accounts." Accounts may be suspended, with notice and an offer to upgrade, for "unusual calling patterns inconsistent with normal, individual use, for example, regular faxes of short duration or faxes to multiple numbers in a short period of time".
budget.page_rule: HumbleFax's terms, read 2026-10-07: "The Company defines one 'fax page' as the greater of 60 seconds of transmission time or one document page." Faxbot counts the same way wherever it knows the time on the line (its own call records, or the transmission time HumbleFax reports for a received fax) and counts pages alone where it does not.
budget.count_sentence: HumbleFax counts each document page or each 60 seconds on the line, whichever is more, and Faxbot counts the same way wherever it knows the time on the line.

providers.label: Phaxio, US and Canada, sending
providers.notes: 7 cents per page in the US and Canada; 5 cents from 50,000 pages a month and 4 cents from 100,000. Numbers are $2 a month. Read again October 7, 2026.

providers.label: Phaxio, US and Canada, receiving
providers.notes: The homepage says send and receive starting at 7 cents per page; caller name is 1 cent more per fax received.

providers.label: Sinch Fax API, sending

providers.label: Sinch Fax API, receiving
providers.notes: The same page is titled Send and Receive Secure Faxes and gives a single flat rate of $0.045 per page with no separate receiving rate, so received pages are read at that rate. Sinch does not publish a price for the fax number.

providers.label: SignalWire Fax, sending
providers.notes: $0.0095 per minute for the 48 contiguous states and Canada. No billing increment is published, so whole minutes is the cautious estimate.

providers.label: SignalWire Fax, receiving
providers.notes: $0.0095 per minute inbound; the number is a voice number at $0.50 a month.

The US page offers the eFax API with eFax Corporate only.

The US page offers the eFax API with eFax Corporate only.

reference_plans.label: eFax Plus plan (Australia)

The page lists the API as available on this plan; confirm with eFax Australia.

reference_plans.label: eFax Pro plan (Australia)
reference_plans.includes: 200 pages sent and 200 received a month
reference_plans.notes: eFax Australia pricing page, read October 4, 2026, prices excluding GST: from $18.95 a month billed monthly or $15.80 a month ($189.90 a year) billed annually, $10 set-up fee, 200 pages sent and 200 received a month, 10 cents per additional page.

reference_plans.label: eFax Pro2 plan (Australia)
reference_plans.includes: 300 pages sent and 300 received a month
reference_plans.notes: eFax Australia pricing page, read October 4, 2026, prices excluding GST: from $23.95 a month billed monthly or $19.95 a month ($239.50 a year) billed annually, $10 set-up fee, 300 pages sent and 300 received a month, 10 cents per additional page.

reference_plans.label: eFax Corporate (API, Australia)
reference_plans.notes: eFax Australia pricing page, read October 4, 2026: eFax Corporate has custom pricing plans. No published price; add your rate.

reference_plans.label: eFax (UK)
reference_plans.notes: eFax UK, read October 4, 2026: the UK site's plan and sign-up links lead to eFax's US price page and a US dollar checkout when read from the US, so no UK price could be read; eFax Corporate in the UK is sold through enterprise.efax.eu by quote. No published price; add your rate.

receiving_prices.label: Telnyx inbound channel, US
receiving_prices.notes: Monthly price of each inbound channel: the first 10 channels at $12, the next 40 at $11, the next 200 at $9 and any beyond 250 at $8. Channels replace per-minute billing for calls received on the numbers that share them. Only standard local numbers can use channels; toll-free and international numbers stay billed by the minute. A call that arrives while every channel is in use hears a busy tone instead of being billed by the minute. Channel-billed and per-minute numbers can be on the same account.

receiving_prices.label: Telnyx received calls, US local number
receiving_prices.notes: Starting rate for calls received on a local number. Telnyx bills 60/60: every call is rounded up to whole minutes, with a one-minute minimum.

receiving_prices.label: Telnyx received calls, US toll-free number
receiving_prices.notes: Starting rate for calls received on a toll-free number, billed in whole minutes.

receiving_prices.label: Telnyx US local number
receiving_prices.notes: From $1 a month. Text messaging on the number costs $0.10 a month more, which a fax number does not need.

receiving_prices.label: Telnyx US toll-free number
receiving_prices.notes: From $1 a month. Text messaging on the number costs $0.10 a month more, which a fax number does not need.

receiving_prices.label: Telnyx SIP trunk
receiving_prices.notes: Telnyx lists a $0 platform fee and pay-as-you-go calls with no contract, so a trunk has no monthly fee of its own.

international.label: AnveoDirect, calls to Canada (Standard route)

The northern territories (+1867) have their own entry.

international.notes: The Standard rate sheet, read October 7, 2026: "Mexico" (52) at $0.00021 a minute, billed in whole minutes; mobile numbers cost $0.002 to $0.0035.

international.label: Flowroute SIP trunk, calls to Canada
international.notes: Flowroute's outbound price covers the lower 48 US states and Canada.

international.label: Telnyx SIP trunk, calls abroad
international.notes: The Elastic SIP price page, read October 7, 2026, lists US prices only and refers to rates by country. Telnyx rates calls by the dialed prefix; download your rate deck from the Outbound Voice Profile in the Telnyx portal and enter the prices for the countries you fax.

international.label: Phaxio, faxes to Canada
international.notes: The price page, read October 7, 2026: "US & Canada" at 7 cents a page.

international.label: Phaxio, faxes outside the US and Canada
international.notes: The price page, read October 7, 2026: "International" at 10 cents a page, one rate for every country.

international.label: Sinch Fax API, faxes abroad
international.notes: The Fax API page, read October 7, 2026, gives a flat $0.045 a page and describes coverage in the U.S.; it does not say whether that price applies abroad. Enter your contracted rate.

toll_free.label: Telnyx SIP trunk, calls to US toll-free numbers
toll_free.t38: Telnyx sends a T.38 re-INVITE once it hears fax tone; when no re-INVITE comes the call continues as G.711 audio.
toll_free.notes: The Elastic SIP price page, read October 7, 2026, lists "Toll Free calls | Free" beside "Local calls | Starting at $0.005 per minute". Telnyx rejects an outbound call whose caller ID is not valid with "403 Caller Origination Number is Invalid D35", and never hides the caller ID on a call to a toll-free number, because "the owner of the toll free number will be paying for the call and therefore has the right to know who is calling them." Caller IDs must be Telnyx numbers or numbers Telnyx verified.

toll_free.label: AnveoDirect, calls to US toll-free numbers (Standard route)
toll_free.t38: AnveoDirect describes only its Prime route as "usually with T.38"; the Standard route may carry the call as audio.
toll_free.notes: The Standard rate sheet, read October 7, 2026, has "USA Toll Free" rows for 800, 844, 855, 866, 877 and 888 at $0.00178 a minute and 833 at $0.00182, all billed per second (1-1). This entry uses $0.00182, the highest of the codes in service. The sheet has no Canadian toll-free rows; Canada uses the same toll-free codes.

toll_free.label: Flowroute SIP trunk, calls to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: Flowroute's caller ID rules, read October 7, 2026: "A customer must utilize a valid, legitimately assigned domestic North American billing Automatic Number Identification (ANI) that's local, and not Toll-Free." An invalid one "may prevent outbound calls from connecting". Its price page lists toll-free receiving ($0.00975 a minute plus a $0.0053 dip charge a call) but no price for calling a toll-free number.

toll_free.label: SignalWire SIP, calls to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: SignalWire's voice price table, read October 7, 2026, lists "Toll Free" at $0.0147 a minute inbound and $0.0069 outbound, by number type. The table prices calls on your own toll-free number, so Faxbot does not read the outbound figure as the price of calling someone else's; that price is not published.

toll_free.label: Sinch Elastic SIP Trunking, calls to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: Sinch shows no Elastic SIP Trunking rates without an account, so the price of calling a toll-free number is not published. Enter your contracted rate.

toll_free.label: Phaxio, faxes to US and Canadian toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: Phaxio prices sending at 7 cents a page in the US and Canada with no exception for toll-free numbers; its FAQ says it can fax "any machine with a 10-digit phone number in the United States or Canada".

toll_free.label: Sinch Fax API, faxes to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: Sinch advertises a "Flat rate of $0.045 per page" with no exception for toll-free numbers; it does not say whether faxes to toll-free numbers are accepted.

toll_free.label: SignalWire Fax, faxes to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: SignalWire's fax price, $0.0095 a minute, is stated for "48 contiguous states of the US and Canada" with separate Alaska and Hawaii rates; it does not say which rate a toll-free number gets.

toll_free.label: HumbleFax, faxes to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: HumbleFax's plan is "Unlimited Faxing $10 / Month" with "No overage fees"; its pages say nothing about toll-free numbers, so a fax to one counts as included in the plan.

toll_free.label: Documo, faxes to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: Documo publishes plan prices ($0.07 to $0.15 an additional page) but nothing about faxes to toll-free numbers.

toll_free.label: eFax Corporate, faxes to toll-free numbers
toll_free.notes: eFax Corporate's FAQ says "Outbound send rates are 10 cents per page to U.S. numbers." with no exception for toll-free numbers, and "Inbound faxes to a toll free number are an additional 2 cents per page." for the receiver. eFax has no rate card in Faxbot, so the cost stays unknown until you add one.

origin_rates_description: Prices by where calls start and the number called (provider-rules design §3.7): route (a card identity), origin (any, a site key, or country:XX), destination_prefix (E.164 digits without the plus; the longest match wins within the most specific origin), prices and billing as on cards (billing "60-60" is minimum seconds, then increment), source and date. pricing not_published records a carrier we looked up that publishes none: its price stays unknown, never zero.
